summary: 1918 steel fire tower on Azure Mountain: staffed to 1978, NRHP-listed 2001, restored by DEC and volunteers, reopened 2003; a 2018 visit found it in good condition.

facts.design: 35-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower with a 7x7-foot metal cab (register); the group's chronology calls the steel galvanized

access.note: Hike of about one mile from a parking lot on Blue Mountain Road, with a 944-foot climb. The 2018 register visit report says the Azure Mountain Friends maintain the trail and tower. No source sets out current rules for the cab, and none confirms that visitors can climb it now. A July 2007 register visit report says the tower was open to the public at that time; that is too old to treat as current.

visit.trail_note: About one mile from the parking lot to the summit, with a 944-foot climb; hiking boots or shoes are recommended

facts.agency: New York Dept. of Environmental Conservation

events.note: First lookout on the site: a wood observation station or platform
Present 35-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower erected; the register says New York DEC built it for $300, the group's chronology says $530; Wikipedia gives 40 feet
Lookout staffed until 1978 per the register
Closed by the DEC; lower two sets of stairs removed to prevent tower access
Tower named to the National Register of Historic Places with six other fire towers; the only one of the seven not yet restored; Azure Mountain Friends formed that fall
Restored by NYSDEC personnel, AmeriCorps workers and Azure Mountain Friends volunteers
Tower officially reopened with a Sept. 27 observance
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register September 30, 2003
NHLR visit report March 11, 2018: good condition, recently painted, glass not intact, not staffed
Centennial of the tower observed July 29, 2018

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the group's chronology both give a 35-foot tower; the Wikipedia station article gives 40 feet. The record uses 35 feet from the two primary accounts and the story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: cost ($300 in the register vs $530 in the group chronology) and height (35 ft vs 40 ft in Wikipedia) disagree; the story reports both and the record keeps the register cost in the event note. The register's elevation (2,500 ft, 762 m) is for the lookout site; mountain heights in other sources differ, but those came from search snippets that were not read, so they are not used. The 2018 visit notes glass not intact; the current condition of the cab and any climbing rules are unverified. Andy Arthur's trail map page returned 403; the Daily Gazette centennial article and the 2003 Azure Mountain News PDF were not read. Brief record's events listed only the 2003 registration; the 1914, 1918, 1978, 2001 and 2002 events were added from sources 1 and 2. A July 5, 2007 register visit report says the tower is currently open for general public use; that is too old to treat as current, so the story does not rely on it.
